prompt.context:
Hyper is a mobile application that connects drivers with passengers. Launched successfully in 2010, it has been experiencing declining profitability for the last year. The COO of Take has requested your services to understand why.

Background: Headquartered in California; services all of North America. One new entrant, Elevate, entered the market in 2013. Mobile phone application for all operating systems that needs to be downloaded by the passenger to link up with drivers in the neighborhood. Pricing is based on a proprietary algorithm which looks at supply of drivers, demand of passengers, and length of the demanded trip. Drivers are not permanent employees of Take, simply contractors. Revenue comes from ride fares and transaction fees.
prompt.question: Take Inc. has been experiencing declining profitability for the last year. Why is profitability declining, and what should the company do about it?

clarifying_info.q: What is the average price of a ride in 2014?
What is the average number of rides taken per customer in 2014?
What is the average price of a ride in 2018?
What is the average number of rides per customer in 2018?
clarifying_info.a: Remains the same as 2014: 50 rides per customer

exhibits.title: Take's Financials Since Launch
exhibits.shows: Two charts. The main chart shows Take's Costs, Revenue, and Profit from 2012 to 2020 in millions of dollars. A smaller chart shows quarterly revenue broken down by season (Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall).
exhibits.data: Costs, Revenue, and Profit figures in $M from 2012 to 2020; seasonal quarterly revenue bars labeled Winter/Spring/Summer/Fall; approximate 2014 revenue ~$300M, 2018 revenue ~$400M; costs rising steadily; profit appears flat after 2014

framework: Ride Revenue: decompose into Price/Fare (algorithm-based on supply, demand, ride length; quality-based pricing) and Quantity (number of rides by length/time/area; number of passengers by location and customer type)

Take Inc. Costs: decompose into Fixed (new investments, corporate office rent, tech infrastructure, salaries, insurance) and Variable (commissions paid to drivers, marketing and advertising to acquire customers and drivers)
Macro / External Factors: inflation, weather/climate, economic downturn, competition (direct competitors, public transit, scooters), regulatory issues

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, what are your first-order observations about Take's financial performance? Calculate the number of rides taken in 2014.
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that profits are flat because costs continue to rise while revenues grow at a slower rate after 2014. Slower revenue growth in 2014 could be attributed to the new entrant Elevate. To calculate rides: Revenue 2014 / Average price per ride.

math.setup: 2014 Revenue = $300M; Average price per ride in 2014 = $15

questions.prompt: Using the 2014 ride count, calculate the total number of customers who took rides in 2014.
questions.guidance: Divide total rides by average rides per customer. Second-order insight: compare to total North American population to estimate penetration rate.

math.setup: Rides in 2014 = 20,000,000; Average rides per customer in 2014 = 50

questions.prompt: Now calculate the number of rides and the number of customers in 2018, then compare to 2014.
questions.guidance: Candidate should note that despite higher revenue in 2018, the price increase to $25 means fewer rides and fewer customers. The ~10% decline in customers is a key profitability driver. Candidate should hypothesize that the $10 price increase likely impacted volume negatively, and that new entrant Elevate may have undercut Take on price, causing customer loss.

math.setup: 2018 Revenue = $400,000,000; Average price per ride in 2018 = $25; Average rides per customer in 2018 = 50 (unchanged)
steps: Change in customers = (320,000 - 400,000) / 400,000 = -20% (note: casebook guidance says ~10%; candidate should flag the discrepancy and reason through it)
math.answer: ~16M rides and ~320,000 customers in 2018; customer base down roughly 10-20% vs. 2014

brainstorming.prompt: After further analysis, the COO concluded that Take is losing customers to Elevate and needs to find a solution to retain customers. How can Take accomplish this?

categories.name: Keep Existing Customers
ideas: Access to special offers or deals (e.g., X rides for $Y)
Personalized deals based on customer profile and data

categories.name: 4Ps – Promotion
ideas: Targeted advertising based on location, customer profile, and media type

categories.name: 4Ps – Pricing
ideas: Competitive pricing to match or undercut Elevate

categories.name: 4Ps – Product
ideas: Accessibility improvements on more operating systems

categories.name: 4Ps – Placement
ideas: Expansion into new cities and countries

categories.name: Second-Order Risks
ideas: Increased customer acquisition and marketing costs
Potentially low ROI on marketing spend

recommendation: Take has seen declining profitability due to a roughly 10% decrease in ride volume, driven by losing customers to competitor Elevate.

Recommendation: implement a targeted marketing campaign to acquire new customers and drive recurring revenue from existing customers through a loyalty/rewards program and competitive pricing adjustments.
risks: Costly to implement marketing and advertising campaigns
Long-term sustainability risk if additional new entrants emerge
Potential lack of internal technological infrastructure to implement solution end-to-end
Risk of price war with Elevate eroding margins further
next_steps: Quantify costs related to launching the marketing plan; explore grassroots or organic (unpaid) options first
Conduct synergy mapping to identify cost reduction opportunities across the value chain
Benchmark pricing against Elevate to understand competitive gap and optimal price point
